turns.content: For the cardioid r=1+sin(theta), identify the cusp and explain why 0<=theta<=2pi traces the curve exactly once.
Set up the polar area integral over that full tracing, including dr/dtheta.
Simplify the integrand using trigonometric identities and state where an absolute value enters.
Use u=theta/2+pi/4 to transform the integral and determine the new limits.
Evaluate the probability mass function obtained after the substitution, splitting its domain wherever the sign changes.
Combine the two pieces and the transformed prefactor, keeping the contributions explicit for a final check.
Verify that the sign split and symmetry are consistent with a nonnegative arc-length integrand over the full curve.
Give the electric capacitance of the cardioid r=1+sin(theta).
